2026–2027 Organization & Management Plan — one club, three teams, and a clear pathway from first training to matchday.

Join the Club → See the Structure
02 · Introduction

Built on passion,
run like a team.

The Xidian University Football Club brings together students who share a passion for football, teamwork, and competition. The club aims to develop players' skills, promote friendship, and create a strong football community at Xidian University.

Led by Mohammed Lamkhayar · Xidian International Football Team
03 · Next Semester Plan

Three teams,
one club.

Team 1

Main Competitive Team

15 players — 11 starters and 4 substitutes. Represents the club in all major competitions and official school events.

Team 2

Development Team

A larger player pool focused on improvement, match experience, and earning promotion to Team 1 through consistent performance.

Girls Team

Women's Squad

A separate female team with its own team leader — adapted training sessions and dedicated preparation for school and Sports Department competitions.

One Identity

All teams share the same values, discipline, and identity. Every player is part of the International Football Club community at Xidian University.

04 · A Competitive Pathway

The team
movement system.

Our promotion and demotion system ensures Team 1 remains competitive while giving every player a clear and fair opportunity to improve. Movement between teams is based on objective criteria.

↑

Team 2 → Team 1

Promotion is earned through strong performance, consistent attendance, physical condition, discipline, and active match participation. Every player has the opportunity to rise.

↓

Team 1 → Team 2

A player may be moved down if attendance, punctuality, commitment, discipline, or performance falls below the required standard. Standards must be maintained.

Performance Attendance Punctuality Commitment Discipline Match Participation

07 · Weekend Match Model

One match,
every weekend.

Managed by Mohammed Lamkhayar, Sami Elhilali & Ayoub Ourain

The club targets one competitive match every weekend so players gain regular match experience — against Chinese student teams, international student teams, university teams, football clubs and external student groups. If no external opponent is available, an internal match between Team 1 and Team 2 keeps everyone match-ready.

Objective: provide consistent competitive experience, develop tactical awareness, and evaluate players for promotion and selection.

08 · Club Competitions

Small tournaments,
real friendships.

The club organizes small football tournaments among its members — a friendly, enjoyable atmosphere where everyone can play, improve, and enjoy the spirit of football together.

09 · Internal Matches

Girls' development
opportunity.

Four girls from the Girls Team may be invited to participate in internal matches between Team 1 and Team 2 — exposing female players to high-intensity, high-pressure match situations beyond regular training, in direct preparation for the school tournament.

Purpose

Expose players to competitive pressure, accelerate development, and build match confidence ahead of school competitions. All internal matches remain organized, competitive, and development-oriented.

10 · Attendance, Respect & Discipline

Commitment holds
the club together.

Lateness — Team 1

Any Team 1 player arriving late is automatically moved to Team 2. Three instances of lateness may result in a ban from the club.

Absence — Team 1

An unjustified absence results in an automatic move to Team 2. Three unjustified absences may result in a ban from the club.

Team 2 Players

Players seeking promotion to Team 1 must demonstrate consistent attendance and punctuality. The same lateness and absence rules apply.

Respect

Players must respect managers, leaders, coaches, training managers, teammates, opponents, and the overall club organization at all times — and follow instructions during training, matches, competitions and all team activities without exception.

Consequence

Repeated refusal to follow instructions, or disrespect toward managers or teammates, will be reviewed. Consequences may include suspension or a permanent club ban.
